honesty_note: The USNO tolerance (120 s) was declared on 2026-10-28 in research/panchanga/reference-fixtures/usno-sunrise-sunset-2026.json, before any sunrise computation. The IMD tolerance reuses that same 120 s rule unchanged; it was not tuned to the IMD results, but it is stated here after a scoping comparison, so QA and the owner must confirm or replace it. The oracle and Swiss-conformance tolerances are engineering bounds derived from the oracle's stated accuracy and from the measured geocentric/topocentric parallax; they are not accuracy claims.

independent_oracle.basis: Meeus low-accuracy Sun (about 0.01 deg) gives a few seconds of time; the band above 40 deg allows for slower horizon crossings

oracle_discrimination.rule: |engine(47') - engine(50')| must exceed the oracle tolerance at every Indian case, so the oracle layer can tell the conventions apart

swiss_rise_trans_geocentric.basis: Swiss-on-Swiss with a different algorithm; Swiss rise_set_fast has no convergence test, so its own residual grows at high latitude

swetest_altitude.rule: |swetest topocentric geometric altitude + solar parallax (8.794148"/R cos h) - (-depression)| at the engine instant
